bifrost: bifrost_ui::model_store (Store: insert, set, fetch, delete, save, rollback), bifrost_ui::relations (Relations, DeleteRule, Relation minimum and maximum counts), bifrost_ui::history (History, Descriptor, Token, Change), bifrost_app::defaults (UserDefaults), bifrost_app::document (NSDocument), bifrost_app::restoration, bifrost_app::file_coordination, bifrost_app::observable, bifrost_ui::undo, springboard/apps/notes-desktop/src/notes/store.rs
summary: SwiftData is a declarative object-graph layer over a store: @Model classes, ModelContainer and ModelContext, predicate queries, relationships, undo, history and iCloud sync. BifrOSt now has a pure in-memory record store with a model-context style API (unique fields, relations with delete rules and count limits, transaction history with tokens, rollback), but no declarative model type, no SDK surface for it, no on-disk store and no sync.

features.feature: Model classes and schema (@Model, Attribute, Unique, Index, Transient)
features.bifrost: none; closest is springboard/sdk/src/coding.rs (Encodable/Decodable, JSON and plist) used by springboard/sdk/src/restoration.rs; springboard/ui/src/model_store.rs declare_unique gives single-field uniqueness
features.note: single-field uniqueness per entity is enforced on every write; no declarative model macro, no schema object, no index constraints, no transient marker; entities and fields are strings

features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/model_store.rs (StoreError: NotFound, Duplicate, Relation); springboard/ui/src/relations.rs (RelationError: Unknown, TooMany, TooFew, Denied); springboard/sdk/src/defaults.rs and springboard/sdk/src/file_coordination.rs (Result-based errors such as CoordinationError::Timeout)
features.note: error types exist per subsystem; no store error taxonomy for storage failures, since the store has no disk layer

gaps: No declarative model layer: no model type, schema, or SDK-level container for persistent objects; bifrost_ui::model_store is not exposed through bifrost_app.
The record store is in memory only: no on-disk format, no store abstraction and no batching.
No predicate or sort-descriptor fetch over records, and no live results that update views.
Relation inverses are not declared; the only inverse lookup is referrers(). Index constraints and multi-field uniqueness do not exist.
No history observer and no persistence or merge of the transaction log, so history-based sync cannot be built on SDK APIs yet.
No iCloud or cross-device sync API for app model data.
Undo does not capture store changes automatically; rollback returns to the last save only.
